runner.text:
**Brief for the coach — where things stand and what's proposed**

**What's in force today**

The engine is running the third version of Joe's program, an amendment adopted on 4 Nov 2026 with a hypertrophy emphasis. The stated reason for that version: the engine update let counted variants (negatives and band pull-ups) give the pull-up a real weekly set target, and let a conditioning session sit on the same day as a lifting day, so the kettlebell swing finisher moved out of Monday's lifting session into its own 12-minute every-minute-on-the-minute session. No warnings came back on any read.

The week: six training days, Thursday off. Monday is OHP, back and arms (75 min) followed by the swing session. Tuesday is the PT at the gym, alternating chest-and-back (roughly 6 chest, 6 lat, 3 biceps sets) with legs-and-core (roughly 6 quad, 4 glute, 4 abdominal sets). Wednesday is pull-up volume and core (75 min, before the lunchtime run). Friday is the strict pull-up test, squat and legs (75 min). Saturday is bench, back and arms (90 min). Sunday is deadlift and legs (90 min). The strength circuit and the daily dead hang (2 × 20 s, easy) are optional.

Targets the program holds itself to: 10 hard sets per muscle per week; 5 sets a week each on bench, overhead press and squat, 4 on deadlift; 10 pull-up sets a week counting negatives and band pull-ups. A deload triggers after at most 6 hard weeks: sets cut 40 %, loads unchanged, nothing past RPE 8, with a test on the main lifts.

**The sessions, exactly as recorded**

- Monday — Overhead Press: warm-ups 1×5 and 1×3, a top set 1×5 at RPE 8, then 4×6 at 85 % of the top set, 3 min rest. Chest-supported dumbbell row 4×8–12 at RPE 8, 2 min rest. Lateral raise 3×12–15 and rear-delt fly 3×12–15, both RPE 8, paired, 60 s rest. Four exercises in total.
- Wednesday — Scapular pull-ups 2×6–8 easy to activate. Negative pull-ups 3×2–4 at RPE 8 with a 4–5 s lower (once every set hits 4, lengthen the lower to 6 s, then 8 s, then add the vest). Band pull-ups 4×5–8 at RPE 8, move to a lighter band once every set hits 8. Flexed-arm hang 2×20 s. Lying leg raise 3×10–15 paired with suitcase carry 4×30 s. Single-leg standing calf raise 3×10–15.
- Friday — One strict pull-up test rep, all-out, one attempt. Back squat warm-ups of 5, 3 and 2, a top set 1×5 at RPE 8, then 4×5 at 85 %, 3 min rest. Romanian deadlift 3×6–10, split squat 3×8–12, dumbbell shoulder press 3×8–12, single-leg calf raise 3×10–15, ab wheel 3×6–12, all RPE 8.
- Saturday — Bench warm-ups of 8, 5 and 3, top set 1×5 at RPE 8, then 4×6 at 85 %. Barbell bent-over row 4×6–10, incline dumbbell bench 3×8–12, dip negatives 3×3–5, overhead triceps extension 3×10–15, lateral raise 3×12–15, all RPE 8.
- Sunday — Deadlift warm-ups of 5 and 3, top set 1×5 at RPE 8, then 3×5 at 85 %. Bulgarian split squat 3×8–12, barbell hip thrust 3×8–12, band pull-ups 3×5–8, dumbbell bicep curl 3×8–12, hammer curl 3×10–12 (all RPE 8), farmer's walk 3×30 s.
- Swings — 12 minutes, 12 swings each minute at RPE 7; the session can grow 2 minutes at a time to 16, and reps can rise to 15.
- Circuit — 4 rounds (up to 6 within a 16-minute cap) of 10 goblet squats, 12 ring push-ups, 12 swings, 16 mountain climbers at RPE 8.

Progress report: no block has closed yet (the program is three days old), so there is nothing to report on lifts, weekly sets or trend. That is expected, not a problem.

**The gap the proposal addresses**

The old program had dumbbell incline curls on both pull days. The new program has no incline curl anywhere. Direct biceps work now is Sunday's 3 sets of curls and 3 sets of hammer curls, plus about 3 sets at the PT on chest-and-back weeks, with rows and pull-ups adding indirect work. Joe's stated preference is that biceps work be dumbbell curls, which this fits.

**What is proposed, and what has actually happened so far**

Proposed: add Incline Curl (Dumbbell), 3 sets of 8–12 at RPE 8, as the fifth and final exercise of Monday's OHP session, on the same double-progression rule as the other accessories (add weight once every set reaches 12).

So far, only an editable copy of the current program has been written out, with no warnings. Nothing has changed in the program or in Hevy. The copy still needs the new line written in — exercise, sets, rest and a one-line reason for the amendment — and ideally a starting load per hand, which has not been chosen yet.

If adopted it would record a fourth program version, as an amendment: the current training block continues rather than resets, Monday goes from four exercises to five, and weekly direct biceps sets rise by 3. A rehearsal pass first shows the exact diff, the start load in pounds with its Hevy kilogram equivalent, and Monday's new time estimate against its 75-minute cap, and writes nothing. Pushing the new line into the Monday routine in Hevy happens only when the next week's plan is approved; that step asks for an explicit yes.

**What Joe needs to agree to**

1. Adding 3 sets of incline curls to the end of Monday, understanding Monday already carries the swing session afterwards and must stay inside about 75 minutes of lifting.
2. The starting load per hand.
3. That this is recorded as an amendment, so the current block and its deload clock carry on unchanged.

first.text:
One thing to settle before I show you the final Monday: the starting weight per hand for the incline curl.

Incline curls are harder than a standing curl at the same load because the stretch at the bottom takes away your momentum, so most people run them a notch lighter than their regular dumbbell curls. If you remember what you were using for them in the old routine, that's the best starting point. Otherwise, tell me what you've been using for Sunday's bicep curls and I'll set the incline curl one dumbbell step down from that.

Once you give me a number, I'll put the line in as the fifth and last exercise on Monday, 3 sets of 8 to 12 at RPE 8, adding weight once every set hits 12, the same rule as the rest of your accessories. Then I'll show you exactly what gets recorded: the full Monday with its time estimate against the 75 minutes, the start weight and its kilogram equivalent for the app, and confirmation that this goes in as a small change to the current program, so your current block and deload clock carry on as they are. Nothing is recorded until you say yes to that, and the new line only goes into your Monday routine in Hevy when you approve next week's plan.
